* * *

In elderly care, one of the most common challenges is ensuring that they take their medications in a timely and accurate manner. Forgetfulness or confusion about dosages can have serious consequences, especially for individuals who must follow complex regimens to treat multiple conditions. Today, Twilio’s technology, combined with artificial intelligence, could offer a revolutionary solution: an automated system that, based on an analysis of the medical history, schedules and sends daily reminders via SMS, WhatsApp, or push notifications can help to improve adherence and, consequently, the wellbeing of our elderly.

## The Solution: Automated Medication Reminder

With the technological advances we have achieved today in data analysis and communication channels, we can envision various solutions to help solve the medication adherence problem for the elderly. Imagine developing an intelligent platform that performs the following functions:

- **Scanning the Medical History:** All medical centers maintain records for each of their patients. These records include relevant information such as age, ailments and diseases, and the medication that is supplied or should be supplied. Medical criteria dictate that medication always depends on different variables like age, condition, and type of medication. Therefore, some medications must be supplied daily, others every two days, and some more than once a day. In designing this solution, AI analyzes the patient’s medical history to identify the prescribed medications, their dosages, and the specific times for administration—all based on medical criteria that allow for a controlled and appropriate assignment of medication according to each patient’s needs.
- **Scheduling Reminders:** With the information gathered from scanning the medical history, different user profiles can be created. Based on this information, automatic reminders are set up and sent to mobile devices via SMS, WhatsApp, or push notifications. The channel can be chosen by each user or according to the preferences registered in their profile.
- **Dose Confirmation:** It is important to emphasize that the goal of this implementation is to have a positive impact on elderly care. Therefore, a crucial step to ensure the desired impact on the patient is to confirm both the receipt of the message and the subsequent confirmation that the medication has been taken correctly by the patient. Accordingly, the system requests a confirmation from the patient or their caregiver, allowing for adherence monitoring. This confirmation is then recorded in the patient’s profile in the database to maintain clear control over the notification and the correct consumption of the medication.
- **Alerts for Caregivers:** As established in this document, the main objective of this solution is the wellbeing of the elderly who are taking the medications. Therefore, functionalities must be implemented that, in case the patient does not confirm taking the medication, trigger an alert to family members or caregivers so that they can intervene promptly. Again, this notification to family members and caregivers will include a confirmation option to help maintain control over the patient’s medical history.

This solution not only focuses on reminding patients about their medication, but it also offers continuous and personalized follow-up, which can make a significant difference in the quality of life and health of elderly people.

![Diagram showing an automated customer response workflow with AI, data, and messaging integration.](https://www.twilio.com/content/dam/twilio-com/global/en/blog/insights/digital-insights-imagery-by-post/a-c/medication-reminders-flow-chart.png/_jcr_content/renditions/compressed-original.webp)

![Diagram showing an automated customer response workflow with AI, data, and messaging integration.](https://www.twilio.com/content/dam/twilio-com/global/en/blog/insights/digital-insights-imagery-by-post/a-c/medication-reminders-flow-chart.png/_jcr_content/renditions/compressed-original.webp)

**Automated Customer Response Workflow with AI, Data, and Messaging Integration**

## Implementation Strategies

To successfully deploy this solution, it is crucial to follow a series of implementation strategies:

**Integration with Electronic Medical Records:**

- **Data Extraction:** Use AI algorithms to extract relevant data from each patient’s digital medical history, such as the name of the medication, dosage, and schedules.
- **Security and Privacy:** Ensure that all data is managed under strict security protocols and complies with data protection regulations, such as HIPAA or GDPR.

**Use of Twilio’s APIs and Solutions**

- **Multichannel Messaging:** Utilize Twilio’s SMS, WhatsApp, and push notification APIs to send reminders on the channel preferred by the user.
- **Twilio Segment:** Employ solutions like Twilio Segment to centralize the data of each user profile and maintain control over the medication supply, which can then be analyzed and processed directly by AI.
- **Functions:** Develop functions that can identify when a user receives and responds to a medication reminder in a timely manner; if not, trigger a new notification to their caregiver, family member, or nurse in charge.
- **Workflow Automation:** Configure automated communication flows that, upon detecting the medication time, activate the timely sending of reminders.

**Personalization Through AI:**

- **Predictive Analysis:** Use machine learning models to predict adherence patterns and dynamically adjust the reminders according to the patient’s behavior. Reviewing the medical history is key, as medical diagnoses may suggest changes in medication that will affect the reminders or require dosage adjustments, which must be considered to vary the periodicity of the reminder notifications.

**User-Friendly and Accessible Interface:**

- **Intuitive Design:** Develop a simple mobile application so that both the elderly and their caregivers can configure, view, and manage the reminders.
- **Multilingual Support:** Ensure that the solution supports multiple languages, facilitating its use in different regions and adapting to the needs of a diverse population.

## Projected Benefits

The development of a solution focused on the elderly aims to improve quality of life and patient interaction by providing technological tools that make the medication process more efficient through the use of advanced Twilio and AI technologies. Some of the most notable benefits include:

- **Improved Adherence:**


Personalized reminders help ensure that patients do not forget their medications, reducing complications and hospitalizations.
- **Peace of Mind for Families:**


Confirmation of medication intake and automatic alerts allow caregivers to stay informed and act quickly in case of any omission.
- **Optimization of Medical Resources:** By reducing the time spent on calls and manual follow-up, healthcare professionals can focus on more critical cases.
- **Continuous Personalization:** AI learns and adapts to individual needs, allowing adjustments to the frequency and content of reminders based on patient behavior.

## Conclusion

Elderly wellbeing can be significantly enhanced through the integration of emerging technologies. The combination of the robustness and flexibility of Twilio’s communication APIs with the predictive and customizable capabilities of artificial intelligence enables the automation of the medication reminder process. This solution not only improves adherence to treatment but also provides greater peace of mind for caregivers and optimizes healthcare resources.

If you are looking to transform the way your patients receive their medication reminders and ensure more rigorous follow-up, now is the time to explore the possibilities offered by Twilio and AI.

Are you ready to innovate in elderly care and improve their quality of life? Technology is here to help you achieve it!

[What is speech recognition and how does it work?](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/ai/what-is-speech-recognition#introduction)

The human voice is a powerful tool for conveying thoughts, emotions, and ideas. While speech has historically been a human trait distinct from machines, the landscape is shifting. Traditionally, our interactions with computers were limited to devices like keyboards and consoles. However, today's advancements in speech recognition software have revolutionized this interaction, enabling seamless communication between people and technology.

Speech recognition technology can be a game-changer for businesses. It can help streamline operations and improve customer experiences with ease. For example, imagine a customer support system that instantly understands and processes customer inquiries without the need for typing. Or an automatic transcription of meetings that can be distributed to everyone who couldn’t attend. Or real-time translations. There are many possibilities, which we’ll discuss below.

In short, speech recognition technology equips businesses with tools to operate more efficiently and engage more effectively, turning spoken words into actionable insights.

## [What is speech recognition technology?](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/ai/what-is-speech-recognition\#toc-heading-38e0a2bc-abcc-4980-9bc3-3dd560fdb076)

Speech recognition is the technology that enables computers and devices to understand and process human speech. It involves converting spoken language into text or commands that a computer can understand and act upon. This technology captures audio input, analyzes the sounds, and matches them to words or phrases in its database to produce an accurate interpretation.

Speech recognition is used in various applications, such as virtual assistants (like [Siri](https://www.apple.com/siri/), [Alexa](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0DCCNHWV5?ref=aucc_web_red_xaa_evgn_tx_0002), or [Google Assistant](https://assistant.google.com/)), customer service bots, transcription services, and more. Its ability to facilitate hands-free interaction with technology not only enhances user convenience but also makes tech more accessible to individuals with physical limitations or those in environments where using hands isn't feasible.

## [How does speech recognition work?](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/ai/what-is-speech-recognition\#toc-heading-f5cc6879-b97c-40cd-b741-5959c7fe171f)

Speech recognition technologies capture the human voice with physical devices like receivers or microphones. The hardware digitizes recorded sound vibrations into electrical signals. Then, the software attempts to identify sounds and phonemes—the smallest unit of speech—from the signals and match these sounds to corresponding text. Depending on the application, this text displays on the screen or triggers a directive—like when you ask your smart speaker to play a specific song and it does.

Background noise, accents, slang, and cross talk can interfere with speech recognition, but advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning technologies filter through these anomalies to increase precision and performance.

Thanks to new and emerging machine learning algorithms, speech recognition offers advanced capabilities:

- [Natural language processing](https://www.twilio.com/docs/glossary/what-natural-language-processing-nlp) is a branch of computer science that uses AI to emulate how humans engage in and understand speech and text-based interactions.

- Hidden Markov Models (HMM) are statistical models that assign text labels to units of speech—like words, syllables, and sentences—in a sequence. Labels map to the provided input to determine the correct label or text sequence.

- N-grams are language models that assign probabilities to sentences or phrases to improve speech recognition accuracy. These contain sequences of words and use prior sequences of the same words to understand or predict new words and phrases. These calculations improve the predictions of sentence automatic completion systems, spell-check results, and even grammar checks.

- Neural networks consist of node layers that together emulate the learning and decision-making capabilities of the human brain. Nodes contain inputs, weights, a threshold, and an output value. Outputs that exceed the threshold activate the corresponding node and pass data to the next layer. This means remembering earlier words to continually improve recognition accuracy.

- Connectionist temporal classification is a neural network algorithm that uses probability to map text transcript labels to incoming audio. It helps train neural networks to understand speech and build out node networks.


## [Speech recognition features to look for](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/ai/what-is-speech-recognition\#5-speech-recognition-features-to-look-for)

Not all speech recognition works the same. Implementations vary by application, but each uses AI to quickly process speech at a high—but not flawless—quality level. Many speech recognition technologies include the same features:

1. Filtering identifies and censors—or removes—specified words or phrases to sanitize text outputs.

2. Language weighting assigns more value to frequently spoken words—like proper nouns or industry jargon—to improve speech recognition precision.

3. Speaker labeling distinguishes between multiple conversing speakers by identifying contributions based on vocal characteristics.

4. Acoustics training analyzes conditions—like ambient noise and particular speaker styles—then tailors the speech recognition software to that environment. It’s useful when recording speech in busy locations, like call centers and offices.

5. [Voice recognition](https://www.twilio.com/blog/what-is-voice-recognition) helps speech recognition software pivot the listening approach to each user’s accent, dialect, and grammatical library.


## [5 benefits of speech recognition technology](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/ai/what-is-speech-recognition\#5-benefits-of-speech-recognition-technology)

The popularity and convenience of speech recognition technology have made speech recognition a big part of everyday life. Adoption of this technology will only continue to spread, so learn more about how speech recognition transforms how we live and work:

1. **Speed:** Speaking with your voice is faster than typing with your fingers—in most cases.

2. **Assistance:** Listening to directions from users and taking action accordingly is possible thanks to speech recognition technology. For instance, if your vehicle’s sound system has speech recognition capabilities, you can tell it to tune the radio to a particular channel or map directions to a specified address.

3. **Productivity**: Dictating your thoughts and ideas instead of typing them out, saves time and effort to redirect toward other tasks. To illustrate, picture yourself dictating a report into your smartphone while walking or driving to your next meeting.

4. **Intelligence:** Learning from and adapting to your unique speech habits and environment to identify and understand you better over time is possible thanks to speech recognition applications.

5. **Accessibility:** Entering text with speech recognition is possible for people with visual impairments who can’t see a keyboard thanks to this technology. Software and websites like Google Meet and YouTube can accommodate hearing-impaired viewers with text captions of live speech translated to the user’s specific language.


## [7 speech recognition use cases for businesses](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/ai/what-is-speech-recognition\#7-speech-recognition-use-cases-for-businesses)

Speech recognition directly connects products and services to customers. It powers interactive voice recognition software that delivers customers to the right support agents—each more productive with faster, hands-free communication. Along the way, speech recognition captures actionable insights from customer conversations you can use to bolster your organization’s operational and marketing processes.

Here are some real-world speech recognition contexts and applications:

1. **SMS/MMS messages:** Write and send SMS or MMS messages conveniently in some environments.

2. **Chatbot discussions:** Get answers to product or service-related questions any time of day or night with chatbots.

3. **[Web browsing](https://www.twilio.com/blog/speech-recognition-browser-web-speech-api):** Browse the internet without a mouse, keyboard, or touch screen through voice commands.

4. **Active learning:** Enable students to enjoy interactive learning applications—such as those that teach a new language—while teachers create lesson plans.

5. **Document writing:** Draft a Google or Word document when you can't access a physical or digital keyboard with speech-to-text. You can later return to the document and refine it once you have an opportunity to use a keyboard. Doctors and nurses often use these applications to log patient diagnoses and treatment notes efficiently.

6. **Phone transcriptions:** Help callers and receivers transcribe a conversation between 2 or more speakers with [phone APIs](https://www.twilio.com/blog/transcribe-phone-calls-text-real-time-twilio-vosk).

7. **Interviews:** Turn spoken words into a comprehensive speech log the interviewer can reference later with this software. When a journalist interviews so

[12 abandoned cart recovery strategies for marketers](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/best-practices/abandoned-cart-recovery-strategies#introduction)

If you don't know how to reduce cart abandonment, you could be leaving money on the table. According to a Baymard Institute analysis, [the average ecommerce company loses 70.19% of checkouts to shopping cart abandonment](https://baymard.com/lists/cart-abandonment-rate). Many of these losses can be recovered by implementing a proactive abandoned cart strategy. Baymard estimates that companies taking steps to improve checkout processes can enjoy a 35.26% increase in conversion rates, while US and EU companies could recover $260 billion annually by prioritizing abandoned cart recovery.

In this blog, we'll show you how to improve cart abandonment rates. We'll explain what abandoned cart recovery is, examine why customers abandon their carts, and discuss how to calculate cart abandonment rate and evaluate cart performance. Then, we'll share 12 abandoned cart best practices to help you convert abandoned carts into successful purchases.

## [What is abandoned cart recovery?](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/best-practices/abandoned-cart-recovery-strategies\#what-is-abandoned-cart-recovery)

To lay a foundation, let's start by answering the basic question: what is cart abandonment recovery? Online shopping cart abandonment occurs whenever a customer initiates a digital checkout but fails to complete the process. Abandoned cart recovery is a proactive strategy for preventing abandonment incidents and intervening when they occur to promote checkout completion.

Abandoned cart recovery strategies consist of steps to reduce abandonment at every stage of the checkout process. These include steps for:

- Preventing abandonment before the checkout process

- Catching abandonment during checkouts

- Responding after abandonment occurs


Strategies for reducing abandonment include improving checkout usability, offering various shipping options, and sending emails and texts to encourage checkout completion. Cart abandonment solutions support these strategies by enabling companies to send [abandoned cart emails](https://www.twilio.com/docs/labs/firebase-extensions/abandoned-cart-emails) and texts and track checkout performance.

Ecommerce companies prioritize abandoned cart recovery because it represents one of the most efficient ways to increase sales. Customers who abandon their carts are already leaning toward making a purchase, making them more likely to buy from you than prospects who haven't even started the checkout process.

You have to invest considerably more time and effort into acquiring new leads and persuading them to buy than you would in salvaging abandoned sales. Making the extra effort to win over customers who abandon their carts can be one of the least costly marketing strategies to generate more revenue.

## [Why do customers abandon their carts?](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/best-practices/abandoned-cart-recovery-strategies\#why-do-customers-abandon-their-carts)

Baymard research (linked above) has identified the top 10 reasons for online shopping cart abandonment. Factoring out window shoppers who were just browsing, the most common reasons customers cited for abandoning their carts were:

01. High extra costs, such as shipping, fees, and taxes (48%)

02. Account creation requirements (26%)

03. Credit card security concerns (25%)

04. Slow delivery times (23%)

05. Long checkout processes (22%)

06. No up-front total calculation (21%)

07. Unsatisfactory return policies (18%)

08. Website errors (17%)

09. Limited payment options (13%)

10. Declined credit cards (9%)


As these results indicate, customers typically abandon carts due to cost, convenience, security, or shipping concerns. Abandoned cart recovery strategies focus on mitigating these issues.

## [How do I calculate cart abandonment rate?](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/best-practices/abandoned-cart-recovery-strategies\#how-do-i-calculate-cart-abandonment-rate)

Shopping cart abandonment rate can be calculated over a given time frame by applying the formula:

    CAR = \[1 – (CC/TC)\] \* 100

Where:

CAR = cart abandonment rate

CC = completed carts

TC = total carts

To illustrate, let's say that over a month, customers opened 1,000 carts and completed 250 purchases:

    CAR = \[1 – (250/1,000)\] \*100 = 75%

In this example, your cart abandonment rate for the month would be 75%.

When interpreting shopping cart abandonment rates, marketing teams should consider them in the context of other factors. For example, the quality and volume of visits can affect rates if your site is attracting window shoppers. Likewise, technical problems with your site or checkout process can increase abandonment rates. To put the cart abandonment rate in context, consider other important key performance indicators (KPIs) such as site speed and conversion rate.

## [What is a good abandoned cart recovery rate?](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/best-practices/abandoned-cart-recovery-strategies\#what-is-a-good-abandoned-cart-recovery-rate)

Baymard's research indicates that cart abandonment rates average 70.19%. This means that, on average, recovering more than 29.81% of abandoned carts reflects an improvement. The average large ecommerce site can increase recovery rates by 35.26% by improving checkout process usability.

Average rates vary by industry, company, and product. For perspective, monitor and benchmark your internal numbers and research competitors' performance.

## [How to reduce cart abandonment](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/best-practices/abandoned-cart-recovery-strategies\#how-to-reduce-cart-abandonment)

Strategies for reducing cart abandonment address common reasons customers abandon carts. Cart abandonment solutions help implement these strategies by streamlining checkout processes, monitoring performance, and supporting recovery emails and texts. Let's look at how to put these strategies into effect.

### [1\. Show clear calls to action (CTAs).](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/best-practices/abandoned-cart-recovery-strategies\#1-show-clear-calls-to-action-ctas)

CTAs can guide customers through the checkout process. This reduces the risk of shoppers abandoning carts over confusion about how to proceed. Use CTAs to:

- Help customers add items

- Initiate checkouts

- Enter shipping and billing information

- Choose shipping options

- Select payment methods

- Complete transactions


### [2\. Display shipping options on your product pages.](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/best-practices/abandoned-cart-recovery-strategies\#2-display-shipping-options-on-your-product-pages)

If customers know their shipping options before they initiate checkout, they're less likely to abandon carts over shipping issues. Allow them to select their shipping location on product pages so they can see the available shipping options.

### [3\. Give customers a guest checkout option.](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/best-practices/abandoned-cart-recovery-strategies\#3-give-customers-a-guest-checkout-option)

Requiring customers to create an account before checking out adds an extra step that can dissuade them from completing transactions. Even customers with accounts may hesitate to check out if they need to spend additional time retrieving credentials and completing login procedures. Simplify your checkout process by allowing customers to check out as guests without logging in.

### [4\. Be transparent about total costs.](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/best-practices/abandoned-cart-recovery-strategies\#4-be-transparent-about-total-costs)

Fees that exceed expectations prompt more customers to abandon carts than any other factor. Avoid sticker shock by being up front about total costs. List itemized costs early in the checkout process so customers can see what they're paying for and choose less expensive options before abandoning orders.

### [5\. Include a thumbnail of cart contents.](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/best-practices/abandoned-cart-recovery-strategies\#5-include-a-thumbnail-of-cart-contents)

Shopping cart thumbnail icons help customers see what's in their cart and what it costs while also enabling them to remove or add items. This reduces the risk of customers abandoning carts due to price concerns or unwanted items. Increase conversions by including a highly visible cart thumbnail image at the top of your customer's user interface.

### [6\. Use analytics to monitor cart abandonment.](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/best-practices/abandoned-cart-recovery-strategies\#6-use-analytics-to-monitor-abandonment)

Analytics tools let you track abandonment activity using KPIs and reports. This enables you to see how often customers are abandoning carts and identify trends that may indicate the reasons for cart abandonment. Ecommerce platforms and shopping cart software typically include these analytics tools.

### [7\. Include progress indicators on the checkout page.](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/best-practices/abandoned-cart-recovery-strategies\#7-include-progress-indicators-on-the-checkout-page)

Progress indicators reassure customers that they're taking the correct steps to complete their purchase, which decreases cart abandonment stemming from confusion about the checkout process. Break your checkout process down into clear steps, such as selecting items, entering addresses, choosing shipping methods, and selecting payment methods. Use indicators to show customers which steps have been completed and which actions still need to be taken.

### [8\. Utilize exit intent pop-ups.](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/best-practices/abandoned-cart-recovery-strategies\#8-utilize-exit-intent-popups)

Exit intent pop-ups are overlays that appear when customers are about to abandon their carts, giving them a second chance to reconsider completing their purchase. Increase the likelihood of conversion by offering incentives like discounts or special offers for finishing their order.

### [9\. Save cart contents.](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/best-practices/abandoned-cart-recovery-strategies\#9-save-cart-contents)

Customers who abandon cart items may have been interrupted by technical problems, distractions at home, or temporary financial issues. In such scenarios, they may be inclined to order the items later when they resume shopping. Give them the opportunity to pick up where they left off by saving the contents of abandoned carts.

### [10\. Offer several payment options.](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/best-practices/abandoned-cart-recovery-strategies\#10-offer-several-payment-options)

Customers may abandon carts if their preferred payment option isn't available. Accommodate them by offering multiple payment options. This can include allowing customers to add multiple credit cards to their account so they can choose which one to use.

### [11\. Create a comprehensive return policy.](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/best-practices/abandoned-cart-recovery-strategies\#11-create-a-comprehensive-return-policy)

Customers may abandon carts if they're concerned about refunds for returned items. Remove this barrier by creating a clear return policy, posting it prominently, and making it easily accessible. Include links to your return policy in page footers, on product pages, and within checkout carts.

### [12\. Send cart recovery emails and texts.](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/best-practices/abandoned-cart-recovery-strategies\#12-send-cart-recovery-emails-and-texts)

Apart from window shoppers, most customers who abandon carts initially had an interest in making a purchase. This presents an opportunity to rekindle their interest by reaching out with email and text offers. Cart abandonment solutions support this strategy by providing tools for automatically sending personalized messages to customers who abandon carts.

To assist you with sending recovery messages, Twilio offers tools for texting and emailing customers, along with [text message examples](https://www.twilio.com/blog/promotional-text-message-examples) and [abandoned cart email templates](https://sendgrid.com/en-us/free-templates/detail/abandoned-cart-email-template/download?utm_referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.twilio.com%2Fen-us%2Fblog%2Finsights%2Fbest-practices%2Fabandoned-cart-recovery-strategies) that you can adapt to your needs.

## [Reduce cart abandonment and re-engage customers](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/best-practices/abandoned-cart-recovery-strategies\#reduce-cart-abandonment-and-reengage-customers) with Twilio

Cart abandonment doesn't have to cut into conversions if you apply the recovery strategies recommended in this article. Successful implementation of these strategies depends on using the right tools.

[Twilio's text marketing solutions](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/solutions/text-marketing) support cart abandonment recovery by enabling you to reengage shoppers with SMS texts. [40+ Content Marketing Best Practices in 2025 (Need to Know)](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices#introduction)

Content marketing best practices don't change too much from year to year, but it's always a good idea to check in every once in a while. Sticking to tried-and-true tips and tactics will help maximize your time, efficiency, and output—it's worth a 5-minute read.

Content marketing—it's like trying to stand out at a rock concert while everyone else is shouting just as loud as you are. With millions of blog posts, videos, and social media updates flooding the internet daily, how do you make sure your content cuts through the noise?

Well, by following the latest-and-greatest content marketing best practices (of course).

Plus, we've collected all the tips and tactics into a single (downloadable) content marketing best practices checklist. You can find it at the bottom of this post, but resist the urge to skip to the end—you'll get the most benefit from digging in top-down.

## [What's the big deal with following best practices?](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#span-stylefontweight-400whats-the-big-deal-with-following-best-practicesspan)

Before we get into the content marketing best practices, let's get on the same page about why all this matters. Content marketing isn't too complicated, right? Create content, and people will come to consume it.

Not quite.

Take a look at these statistics:

- There are more than [600 million blogs](https://growthbadger.com/blog-stats/) on the internet.
- WordPress users post approximately [70 million new posts](https://www.envisagedigital.co.uk/number-blog-posts-published-daily/) on the platform every month (and that's only one of _many_ content management platforms).
- YouTube publishers upload [500 hours of video content](https://www.tubefilter.com/2019/05/07/number-hours-video-uploaded-to-youtube-per-minute/) to the platform every minute.
- Users post over [95 million photos and videos](https://www.zippia.com/advice/instagram-statistics/#:~:text=At%20least%2095%20million%20photos,follow%20at%20least%20one%20business.) on Instagram each day.

Mind-boggling, right? With all that new content emerging daily, how in the world will your audience find _your_ content—and why should they?

You have something special to share: something your audience needs. However, they'll never find it if you don't follow the content marketing best practices outlined below.

## [Benefits of following content best practices](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#span-stylefontweight-400benefits-of-following-best-practicesspan)

Here are a few ways content marketing best practices help improve your overall content program:

- **Eliminate waste:** Without plans and processes, you'll likely waste time creating duplicate content and building content pieces that don't align with your overall marketing strategy.
- **Avoid shiny object syndrome:** It's easy to get distracted when creating digital marketing content—I received a dozen [emails](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/products/email-api), [text](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/messaging), and Slack notifications just while outlining this piece. However, not every distraction, emerging marketing channel, or content trend is worth your time. Sticking to the best practices will keep you on track and aligned with your [content marketing strategy](https://sendgrid.com/en-us/blog/content-marketing-strategy-guide?utm_referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.twilio.com%2Fen-us%2Fblog%2Finsights%2Fcontent-marketing-best-practices). This will also help you [stop procrastinating](https://www.mindthatbear.com/posts/how-to-stop-procrastinating) and start getting real work done.
- **Maximize efficiency:** There are only so many hours in a day—juice them for all they're worth. When you follow these best practices, you cut out the fluff and stick to grounded principles. And that's a surefire strategy for maximum productivity.
- **Think outside the box:** Understanding the best practices unlocks creative freedom to break conventional rules and think outside the box. It's like when an author breaks traditional grammar rules and gets applauded for it (we're looking at you, “The Road”).
- **Build routines:** Workflows and templates will keep you on track and help you produce content at a faster pace.
- **Establish routines:** Revisiting best practices can help you identify bad habits and build new routines that serve you and your content better.

## [40 content marketing best practices in 2025](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#span-stylefontweight-40030-content-marketing-best-practices-in-2023span)

While these content marketing best practices aren't necessarily in order of importance, it’s best to follow them sequentially. Start at the top and work your way down.

### [1\. Identify your target audience](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#span-stylefontweight-4001-identify-your-target-audiencespan)

Content marketing starts with your audience. Start somewhere else, and you're destined to build amazing things that nobody wants—Cheetos lip balm, anyone?

First, choose the buyer persona you want to target. Don't have that yet? Start with [lead nurturing](https://sendgrid.com/en-us/blog/lead-nurturing?utm_referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.twilio.com%2Fen-us%2Fblog%2Finsights%2Fcontent-marketing-best-practices) and the [customer lifecycle](https://sendgrid.com/en-us/blog/customer-lifecycle-marketing?utm_referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.twilio.com%2Fen-us%2Fblog%2Finsights%2Fcontent-marketing-best-practices).

Your content strategies might target different audiences and buyer persona, and that's OK. Just ensure you have a specific reader in mind when writing an article.

Take this blog post, for example. Twilio SendGrid caters to [marketers](https://sendgrid.com/solutions/email-marketing/?utm_referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.twilio.com%2Fen-us%2Fblog%2Finsights%2Fcontent-marketing-best-practices) and [developers](https://docs.sendgrid.com/for-developers). However, developers don't care much about content marketing best practices—that's why I wrote this for you, marketers.

### [2\. Map out your buyer's journey](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#span-stylefontweight-4002-map-out-your-buyers-journeyspan)

You likely have a fictional customer journey in mind for your customers: the customer reads your tweet, laughs, follows your brand, sees more content, then buys your product.

In reality, it's rarely that straightforward (or linear).

Customer journey mapping helps you learn the real path your buyers take, from becoming completely unaware to brand ambassadors of your products.

Plus, customer journeys tend to follow the same stages:

- Awareness
- Consideration
- Purchase
- Retention
- Advocacy

Understanding what each stage looks like for your customers will help you make optimizations to improve it.

Don't have a customer journey yet? [Follow our how-to guide to get started](https://sendgrid.com/en-us/blog/customer-journey-and-email-marketing?utm_referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.twilio.com%2Fen-us%2Fblog%2Finsights%2Fcontent-marketing-best-practices).

### [3\. Build a content marketing strategy](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#span-stylefontweight-4003-build-a-content-marketing-strategyspan)

Without a well-defined content marketing strategy, you're just throwing darts at the board and hoping something sticks. While that can score you some short-term wins, it's not a recipe for long-term success.

Successful content marketing campaigns start with a plan.

You need a reliable, scalable strategy you can trust. And a solid content marketing plan ensures that every piece of content has a purpose and that every purpose aligns with a greater organizational goal.

Read [_How to Create a Content Marketing Strategy in 11 Steps_](https://sendgrid.com/en-us/blog/content-marketing-strategy-guide?utm_referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.twilio.com%2Fen-us%2Fblog%2Finsights%2Fcontent-marketing-best-practices) to start building your plan.

### [4\. Form a world-class content marketing team](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#span-stylefontweight-4004-form-a-worldclass-content-marketing-teamspan)

Top-notch content requires a world-class team, so focus on building a flexible, resilient content marketing team. Find folks with a wide variety of specialties:

- Graphic design
- Video
- Top-of-funnel content
- Search engine optimization (SEO)
- Copywriting
- Long-form content
- Webinars
- Social media management

Don't be afraid to find freelancers and contractors to supplement your content needs. They can be great at filling skill gaps or keeping up with fluctuating demand.

### [5\. Determine key performance indicators (KPIs)](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#span-stylefontweight-4005-determine-key-performance-indicators-kpisspan)

From the get-go—not later—you need to decide what business goals will be crucial to your team. You can't do everything, so get [hyper-focused on a handful of metrics](https://sendgrid.com/en-us/blog/understanding-email-metrics?utm_referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.twilio.com%2Fen-us%2Fblog%2Finsights%2Fcontent-marketing-best-practices) you want to tackle:

- Lead generation
- Organic traffic
- Sign-ups
- Sales
- Awareness

Ensure your content aligns with your marketing goals—not the other way around. For example, content teams often make the mistake of coming up with "good ideas" before creating goals. This leads to amazing content that nobody wants or results your business doesn't need (or care about).

### [6\. Audit your existing content](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#span-stylefontweight-4006-audit-your-existing-contentspan)

Before you start thinking of new content you want to create, take a look at your existing library. You'll likely find heaps of great articles, videos, and graphics that just need a bit of tender loving care to perform well.

For example, you might find a 3,000-word blog post getting little-to-no traffic. Identify keywords it might rank for on page 2 or 3 of Google's search engine results pages (SERPs), and optimize it to try and rank for page 1. It'll take you 10% of the time of creating a new piece—and it’ll start ranking faster too.

### [7\. Identify content gaps](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#span-stylefontweight-4007-identify-content-gapsspan)

While auditing your existing content library, look for gaps. What potential topics have you not covered yet? Do competitors create content you don't have?

Understanding your content gaps gives you an excellent place to start when researching new pieces. For example, do you lack how-to tutorials for your products? Do you need a starter video for the onboarding process?

### [8\. Repurpose content](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#span-stylefontweight-4008-repurpose-contentspan)

You can likely repurpose every piece of content you create. Whether an article, video, or podcast, there are dozens of ways you can repurpose your content in different formats.

Let's take a podcast, for example. Here are a few ways you could repurpose a podcast episode:

- Transcribe your podcast and publish it as a blog post
- Highlight the top takeaways and quotes and publish them as a blog post
- Create graphics with quotes from your podcast episode to publish on social media
- Film your podcast episodes and publish them as YouTube or Vimeo videos
- Create a roundup post highlighting your best podcast episodes
- Make an email series based on lessons from your podcast
- Highlight takeaways in a SlideShare or slide deck
- Turn a podcast episode into a webinar presentation
- Publish podcast quotes on your Instagram, YouTube, and Facebook stories

Need more ways to repurpose content? We've got 20 of them. Check out [_20 Simple Ways to Repurpose Content to Boost Your Traffic_](https://sendgrid.com/en-us/blog/how-to-repurpose-content?utm_referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.twilio.com%2Fen-us%2Fblog%2Finsights%2Fcontent-marketing-best-practices).

### [9\. Remember SEO](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#span-stylefontweight-4009-remember-seospan)

Every piece of content you create can be multipurpose. For example, you might create a product-focused blog post about a new feature you're releasing. That's fine—your current audience will love that. However, you'll likely need to optimize this piece for search engines if you ever want anyone outside your existing customers to learn about it.

Get comfortable doing basic keyword research and finding your users' search queries. Basic SEO best practices can take your content the extra mile.

### [10\. Create different types of content](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#span-stylefontweight-40010-create-different-types-of-contentspan)

Sometimes, content teams get stuck in a rut of producing the same content, whether blog posts, guides, or social media campaigns. Think outside the box and branch out. There's a whole wide world of [content opportunities](https://sendgrid.com/en-us/blog/types-of-email-content-ideas?utm_referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.twilio.com%2Fen-us%2Fblog%2Finsights%2Fcontent-marketing-best-practices)—experiment every once in a while to see if something clicks.

Here's a quick list of different content formats you could produce:

- Blog posts
- Guides
- E-books
- Podcasts
- Infographics
- Webinars
- White papers
- Email campaigns
- Videos
- PDFs
- Presentations
- Templates
- Calculators
- Tutorials
- Interviews
- Case studies

### [11\. Build backlinks](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#span-stylefontweight-40011-build-backlinksspan)

Your site's backlinks and domain authority will impact how well it ranks on SERPs. Fortunately, content creation and backlink building go hand in hand. Look for ways to use content to create high-quality backlinks.

Here are a few content-creation strategies for building backlinks:

- **Create skyscraper content:** There's a lot of _meh_ content on the internet. Create the best-of-the-best pieces on topics to rank high and earn links back to your content organically.
- **Publish original research:** Everyone loves hard facts and data. Instead of regurgitating statistics from around the internet, do your research. It doesn't need to pass any standard deviations or anything—it could be a customer survey on LinkedIn.
- **Offer to guest post:** Offer to publish content on other authority websites and partner pages in exchange for backlinks to your website.
- **Use infographics:** Provide publicly usable infographics and ask for people to link back to your website when they use them.

### [12\. Create templates for success](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#span-stylefontweight-40012-create-templates-for-successspan)

When you find something that works, scale it. For example, if you have a handful of articles that outperform all the rest (which is often the case), decipher any similarities and what makes them perform well.

Do the articles follow a certain format? Does the writing center on specific topics?

Once you find the keys to success, [turn them into a replicable template](https://sendgrid.com/free-templates/?utm_referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.twilio.com%2Fen-us%2Fblog%2Finsights%2Fcontent-marketing-best-practices). For example, you might discover listicles perform best on your website or find top-of-funnel "what is" content works best.

Scale your successes and juice them for all you can.

### [13\. Maintain a content calendar](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#span-stylefontweight-40013-maintain-a-content-calendarspan)

A content calendar (or even an editorial calendar) will keep your content production and publishing schedule on track. Managing handfuls of writers and projects simultaneously can get messy—especially if you don't use a task management system.

Without a content calendar, you'll end up with some weeks where you publish an overwhelming amount of content and others that experience content droughts. You want consistency.

A content calendar ensures every new piece of content gets the time and space it deserves. That means you might publish 1 piece every day or 2 a week. Use a content calendar to stick to whatever cadence you decide on.

### [14\. Target customer pain points](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#span-stylefontweight-40014-target-customer-pain-pointsspan)

You want the content you create to solve problems. Think about questions your customers might have or issues your products help solve. Once you identify the pain point, solve it with content.

Your solution might not always be the primary answer, and that's OK. For example, if you sell fitness equipment, you might create motivational content to inspire your community to work out. _Or_ if you sell email services, you might create content marketing best practice articles to help your customers understand how email works together with content marketing.

See what I did there?

### [15\. Focus on creating valuable content](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#span-stylefontweight-40015-focus-on-creating-valuable-contentspanbb)

Content teams get pressured to create, create, create. With a never-ending to-do list, getting pulled into the publish, publish, publish mindset is easy. However, it's vital to take a step back every once in a while and ask:

- "Where's the value in this piece?"
- "Do my customers _really_ need this piece of content?"
- "Could I spend my time on something more important?"
- "What would happen if I _didn't_ publish this content?"

Questions like these will help you discover if your content is valuable or just busy work.

### [16\. Watch your frequency](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#span-stylefontweight-40016-watch-your-frequencyspan)

[Frequency](https://sendgrid.com/en-us/blog/fighting-email-fatigue-when-is-your-email-frequency-too-high?utm_referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.twilio.com%2Fen-us%2Fblog%2Finsights%2Fcontent-marketing-best-practices) isn't so much about quality over quantity (though we'll get into that soon). It’s more about how often you publish on different channels.

More (even if it's quality) isn't always better.

For example, your customers might love your monthly email newsletter, but that _doesn't_ mean they'd love it more as a weekly newsletter. The same goes with any medium. Just because you can publish a YouTube video every day doesn't mean you should.

Your audience leads busy lives. They have work, family, and personal ambitions to go after. Keep that in mind when you produce content. Don't overwhelm your customers to the point where they can't consume all your content (even if they want to).

### [17\. Get permission](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#span-stylefontweight-40017-get-permissionspanbb)

Believe it or not, not _everyone_ wants to consume your content. Shocking, right? Yet, they won't always get to choose, especially when you use traditional media, video advertisements, or pay-per-click ads to get in front of them.

However, on channels they do get to choose, ensure you get permission before marketing to them. For example, email and [SMS](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/messaging) are opt-in marketing channels. Just because you have your customer's email address from a purchase order or delivery update request doesn't mean you have permission to send them marketing messages.

They need to give you " [unambiguous consent](https://sendgrid.com/en-us/blog/general-data-protection-regulation-what-senders-need-to-know#:~:text=have%20provided%20clear%2C-,unambiguous%20consent,-to%20receive%20them?utm_referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.twilio.com%2Fen-us%2Fblog%2Finsights%2Fcontent-marketing-best-practices)."

Follow [these opt-in options](https://sendgrid.com/resource/build-an-email-list-from-scratch/#:~:text=4.%20Choose%20the%20right%20email%20list%20opt%2Din%20option?utm_referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.twilio.com%2Fen-us%2Fblog%2Finsights%2Fcontent-marketing-best-practices) to learn more about getting subscribers (the right way). Also, brush up on [General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)](https://sendgrid.com/en-us/blog/general-data-protection-regulation-what-senders-need-to-know?utm_referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.twilio.com%2Fen-us%2Fblog%2Finsights%2Fcontent-marketing-best-practices) laws to ensure your email program is compliant.

### [18\. Stay up to date on trends and algorithm changes](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#span-stylefontweight-40018-stay-up-to-date-on-trends-and-algorithm-changesspan)

Content marketing is an ever-changing field. Trends come and go, algorithms change, and new channels flare up and perish months later. It's up to you to stay on top of things to capitalize on shifts.

I remember when I started listening to podcasts about 8 years ago. Even then, I thought I had already missed the podcast bandwagon—and look where we are now.

### [19\. Experiment with new channels](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#span-stylefontweight-40019-experiment-with-new-channelsspan)

Even if it doesn't go according to plan, don’t be afraid to try a new tactic and channel—it's a learning experience. Plus, it's a solid excuse to secure your brand's name and tag on possible digital channels.

You might think a channel might not align with your brand, but you'd be surprised. Just about any company can find success on platforms ranging from Instagram to TikTok to Reddit. There's a good chance your audience uses these different platforms, and that means there's an opportunity for you to reach them there.

The challenge comes from creating relevant content for each channel that your audience _wants_. That's no small feat (and definitely beyond the scope of this article).

Here are a few channels to consider experimenting with (if you haven't already):

- Email
- Social media
- Medium
- LinkedIn
- Reddit
- TikTok
- Quora
- SMS
- Public relations
- Myspace (yes, it still exists)

### [20\. Improve the user experience](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#span-stylefontweight-40020-improve-the-user-experiencespan)

Good content doesn't get the love it deserves if the user experience (UX) suffers. Everything from your site's user interface (UI) to the page's color scheme to accessibility concerns can impact the user experience, and it's a shame when these elements destroy quality content.

Work with your UI/UX team to improve these factors on your website. Test how different layouts affect bounce rates and completion rates. Then, keep working to improve your content's experience to increase the likelihood that customers consume, enjoy, and share it.

### [21\. Focus on quality over quantity](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#span-stylefontweight-40021-focus-on-quality-over-quantityspan)

I told you we'd get here eventually. When it comes to content, quality is always better than quantity. Often, you don't need 5 small blog posts—you just need one big comprehensive one.

The same is true for almost all content you produce. Don't worry about how much of it you create—instead, measure each piece's impact.

Push back against management if they set content creation goals. [Content creation](https://sendgrid.com/en-us/blog/email-content-creation-best-practices?utm_referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.twilio.com%2Fen-us%2Fblog%2Finsights%2Fcontent-marketing-best-practices) isn't your end goal—it's results. And who cares if you drive results with 3 videos or 15 videos?

### [22\. Embrace trends (but show equal love to evergreen content)](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#span-stylefontweight-40022-embrace-trends-but-show-equal-love-to-evergreen-contentspan)

While it’s cool to jump on new trends, never forget about evergreen content. Evergreen content is always relevant. It might not get increased attention or features in headlines, but it's something your audience will always want.

Let's look at email, for example. Right now, everyone cares about artificial intelligence (AI) assisting with email creation. That's fine and relevant, but do you know what email marketers will _always_ search for?

1. [Tips for staying out of the spam folder](https://sendgrid.com/en-us/blog/10-tips-to-keep-email-out-of-the-spam-folder?utm_referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.twilio.com%2Fen-us%2Fblog%2Finsights%2Fcontent-marketing-best-practices)
2. [Email subject line best practices](https://sendgrid.com/en-us/blog/29-best-email-subject-lines?utm_referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.twilio.com%2Fen-us%2Fblog%2Finsights%2Fcontent-marketing-best-practices)
3. [Email design best practices](https://sendgrid.com/resource/email-design-best-practices-for-2019/?utm_referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.twilio.com%2Fen-us%2Fblog%2Finsights%2Fcontent-marketing-best-practices)

Interest in topics like [AI-based email marketing](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/ai-based-email-marketing) and [Brand Indicators for Message Identification (BIMI)](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/what-is-bimi) will rise and fall, but evergreen topics will always be important to your community.

### [23\. Combine content types](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#span-stylefontweight-40023-combine-content-typesspan)

You can stretch the life of every piece of content you produce by looking for ways to combine it with other content types. For example, you might mix and match your content by adding a video to a blog post or using a new e-book in a webinar presentation.

### [24\. Back everything up with data](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#span-stylefontweight-40024-back-everything-up-with-dataspan)

It’s always best not to make claims unless you can back them up with data. For example, I can't just say [email marketing](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/products/marketing-campaigns) is the best distribution channel without also including a statistic like, "Email marketing produces a high return on investment with a [$38 return on every dollar spent](https://sendgrid.com/email-marketing-guide/#:~:text=Yes.%20When%20executed%20thoughtfully%20and%20with%20best%20practices%20in%20mind%2C%20email%20marketing%20can%20convert%20prospects%20into%20customers%20at%20an%20impressive%20rate.%20Email%20marketing%20produces%20a%20high%20return%20on%20investment%20with%20a%20%2438%20return%20on%20every%20dollar%20spent.?utm_referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.twilio.com%2Fen-us%2Fblog%2Finsights%2Fcontent-marketing-best-practices)."

Look for any claims you make in your writing, and find data to support them. Dig deep down the research rabbit hole to ensure it's an accurate, legit statistic and not a regurgitated hoax without any original research.

### [25\. Tie every piece of content to a specific goal](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#span-stylefontweight-40025-tie-every-piece-of-content-to-a-specific-goalspan)

Ideally, before you create it, connect every piece of content to a specific business goal. Will this content drive traffic or help build leads? Do we want this content to build brand awareness or drive sales?

If you can't find a business goal to support your desired content, put it in the backlog. You might find a purpose for that content idea later, but stick with content creation that supports your immediate KPIs and metrics.

### [26\. Use (don't abuse) AI](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#span-stylefontweight-40026-use-dont-abuse-aispan)

AI writers and graphic generators are emerging. These tools can help create original content, build outlines, answer questions, and write articles. However, these are still in the infancy stage, and you should avoid over-relying on them.

Don't be afraid to use AI—just don't abuse it. Let it inspire and give you ideas, but don't think it can replace your content marketing team. It can't.

Need ideas for using AI? Try these [AI-based email marketing use cases](https://sendgrid.com/en-us/blog/ai-based-email-marketing?utm_referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.twilio.com%2Fen-us%2Fblog%2Finsights%2Fcontent-marketing-best-practices).

### [27\. Collaborate with other teams](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#span-stylefontweight-40027-collaborate-with-other-teamsspan)

It's easy for your content marketing team to become a silo. With so much going on and never-ending demand for content, collaboration often gets pushed aside.

Think of teams you could partner with to bolster your effective content marketing efforts. For example, you might work with product marketing or sales to identify content to support their needs or get help from your developers to write more technical-focused content.

### [28\. Redirect or delete content when necessary](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#span-stylefontweight-40028-redirect-or-delete-content-when-necessaryspan)

Old content can start to pile up. While often a vanity metric, lots of underperforming, outdated content just takes up space and accumulates cobwebs.

If you can’t revive, optimize, or repurpose a piece, it's time to get rid of it.

It'll be hard. You might tear up a bit, and that's OK. If you can't do it yourself, work with a partner who can identify content pieces that need to go objectively.

You can do this. We believe in you.

### [29\. Follow the 80/20 content distribution rule](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#span-stylefontweight-40029-follow-the-8020-content-distribution-rulespan)

The [80/20 content rule](https://sendgrid.com/en-us/blog/content-marketing-strategy-guide#:~:text=Follow%20the%2080,mean%20they%E2%80%99ll%20come.?utm_referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.twilio.com%2Fen-us%2Fblog%2Finsights%2Fcontent-marketing-best-practices) suggests you spend:

- **20% of your time** creating content
- **80% of your time** promoting and distributing content

When you publish new content, give it the promotional love it deserves. Just because you post something doesn't mean your audience will read or watch it—they likely won't know it exists.

Use the following promotional channels to distribute every piece of content you produce better:

- Email
- Social media
- Display ads
- Internal linking
- Webinars
- Content bundles
- Podcast notes
- Quora
- Video descriptions

### [30\. Make your content accessible](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#span-stylefontweight-40030-make-your-content-accessiblespan)

Around 1.3 billion people live with some visual impairment—that could be a massive part of your audience. And even if it's not, creating accessible content is just the right thing to do.

Think about [accessibility design best practices](https://sendgrid.com/en-us/blog/email-accessibility-design-best-practice-tips?utm_referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.twilio.com%2Fen-us%2Fblog%2Finsights%2Fcontent-marketing-best-practices), and ensure you add the small touches that make your content widely consumable. For example, add descriptive alt text to your images, and consider providing American Sign Language (ASL) interpretation online when [hosting virtual events](https://sendgrid.com/en-us/blog/accessibility-for-virtual-events?utm_referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.twilio.com%2Fen-us%2Fblog%2Finsights%2Fcontent-marketing-best-practices).

### [31\. Optimize for voice search](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#toc-heading-dd647da9-2f79-4104-b37b-207d475a6d0f)

"Hey Alexa, how do I optimize my content for voice search?"

Voice search isn't just coming...it's already here, and it's changing how people find your content. With smart speakers in millions of homes and voice assistants built into virtually every smartphone, optimizing for voice search isn't negotiable anymore.

Voice searches are fundamentally different from typed queries. They're conversational, question-based, and typically longer. When someone types, they might search "best email marketing platform." But when they speak, it becomes "What's the best email marketing platform for small businesses?"

Here's how to make your content voice-search friendly:

- **Think in questions:** Structure content around the actual questions your audience asks—Who, What, When, Where, Why, and How.
- **Get conversational:** Write like you talk (but still professional)—voice searches use natural language.
- **Target long-tail keywords:** Voice searches are typically 3-5 words longer than text searches.
- **Create structured FAQ sections:** These directly answer common voice queries and are perfect for featured snippets.
- **Consider local intent:** Many voice searches have local intent ("near me" queries), so include geographic terms if relevant.
- **Focus on featured snippets:** Voice assistants often pull answers from position zero—those coveted featured snippets at the top of search results.

### [32\. Focus on interactivity](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#toc-heading-33cf7671-576c-484f-92c6-8a3f4c276171)

Gone are the days when content was just a one-way street. Static content? Boring. Today's audience doesn't want to just read your stuff. They want to play with it, manipulate it, and make it their own.

Interactive content flat-out performs better. Quizzes, calculators, polls, and interactive infographics don't just capture attention; they hold it hostage (in the best possible way, of course).

**Think about it:** Which would you rather consume: a 2,000-word article about email deliverability rates or an interactive tool that analyzes your specific sending patterns and gives you personalized recommendations?

Yeah, me too.

Create calulators, add quizzes, ask for feedback, enable comments, incorporate sliders and toggles.

This is where you go all in on whozits, whatzsits, and thingamabobs.

### [33\. Clean up (read: delete) blog posts](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#toc-heading-61f71530-8b84-4b87-97a2-7469cee7b821)

Your blog has some deadweight. It doesn't take an SEO expert or outside consultant to see that. Don't panic, though. You're not alone. We all get to that point sometimes, and it's okay.

Well, as long as you do something about it, that is.

For example, we've deleted, archived, and redirected hundreds of blog posts over the last year or so (and we plan to do a lot more).

Yes, the vanity metric of number of posts surely takes a hit, but you know what doesn't? Our traffic.

Now, you know those posts: the ones gathering digital dust in the corners of your site, bringing down your averages, and making Google question your content quality. It's time for some tough love.

By removing underperforming content, you're actually helping your best stuff rank higher. Think of it like thinning out seedlings to let the strongest plants thrive.

The 80/20 rule applies perfectly here: roughly 20% of your content likely drives 80% of your traffic. The rest? It's just taking up space and diluting your site's authority. Ouch, but true.

We get it. Getting over your emotional attachment to content you worked hard to create. That post from 2019 about email trends might have been your baby, but if it's getting two visits a month and contains outdated advice, it's time to let it go.

### [34\. Consider the entire funnel](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#toc-heading-250926d8-5481-4604-a981-ee017efb2223)

Your content strategy has a serious middle-child syndrome. Let me guess: tons of top-of-funnel awareness pieces, a decent chunk of bottom-funnel conversion content, but that middle section? Crickets.

You're not alone. Most content marketers are addicted to vanity metrics like page views (hello, top-of-funnel) or obsessed with conversion rates (bottom-funnel), leaving the critical consideration stage abandoned like a shopping cart on a discount website.

Your audience isn't ready to buy after reading one "what is" blog post, and that case study isn't going to magically appear in front of someone who doesn't know they have a problem. The content journey is real, folks.

Your funnel needs content at every stage:

- **Top-of-funnel:** Yes, keep your educational blog posts, thought leadership, and trend reports—they build awareness.
- **Middle-of-funnel:** This is your secret weapon—comparison guides, detailed how-tos, expert interviews, and product tours that help prospects evaluate options.
- **Bottom-of-funnel:** Customer stories, detailed pricing content, implementation guides, and ROI calculators that seal the deal.
- **Post-purchase:** Onboarding content, advanced usage guides, and community resources that prevent churn and create advocates.

Unfortunately, here's where most companies mess up: they create these pieces in isolation, with no clear path from one stage to the next. You need deliberate content pathways that guide readers logically through the buyer's journey.

Think of it like a Netflix series—each episode should leave viewers wanting the next one. Your awareness piece should naturally lead to consideration content, which should make the case for conversion content.

### [35\. Start using generative AI](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#toc-heading-40797868-9f2c-4ead-bd34-b03b9bd57c3b)

You're either using AI tools for content creation or you're falling behind. There's no middle ground anymore.

The initial response to AI was predictable: "But it can't match human creativity!" True...and also completely missing the point. AI isn't meant to replace your creative process—it's meant to accelerate it, handle the grunt work, and let your team focus on what humans do best: strategic thinking and emotional connection.

The key is finding the right human-AI balance. The best content teams use AI as a superpower, not a replacement. They feed the AI their brand voice guidelines, provide specific prompts with context, and then edit the output with their human expertise.

The quality gap between AI early adopters and laggards is widening faster than most marketing leaders realize.

Yes, there are ethical considerations. Yes, you should disclose AI usage when appropriate. And yes, you should have clear guidelines about fact-checking and quality control. But sitting on the sidelines isn't an option anymore.

### [36\. Add content governance frameworks](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#toc-heading-9b21388e-28a8-4a74-844e-73db430a8e71)

Remember when your content operation was just you and a WordPress login? Those were simpler times. Now you've likely got freelancers, agencies, subject matter experts, and that intern who keeps publishing things without approval.

Content chaos isn't just annoying—it's expensive. Without proper governance, you're practically begging for inconsistent messaging, compliance nightmares, and the inevitable "who approved THAT?" moment during the executive review.

Think of content governance as the guardrails that keep your content machine from driving off a cliff. It's not about bureaucracy. It's about creating systems that scale without sacrificing quality.

Here's what a solid content governance framework looks like:

- **Clear roles and permissions:** Who can create, edit, approve, and publish? Document this before someone publishes the unfinished draft with placeholder text that reads "INSERT LEGAL DISCLAIMER HERE."
- **Standardized workflows:** Map out exactly how content moves from idea to publication, with defined checkpoints for SEO, legal, brand, and subject matter expert reviews.
- **Brand and style guidelines:** Create a living style guide that evolves with your brand but maintains consistency across channels and creators.
- **Content auditing protocols:** Establish regular reviews of existing content to identify update needs, consolidation opportunities, and retirement candidates.
- **Compliance documentation:** Track who approved what and when—your legal team will thank you when that random blog post from three years ago suddenly becomes relevant in a dispute.
- **Emergency protocols:** Define exactly who can publish what during a crisis, because that's not the time to be figuring out approval chains.

### [37\. Test out micro-content strategies](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#toc-heading-78302065-2773-4f54-ab83-302e40ceaf4d)

Not everyone has time for your 3,000-word epic guides. There, I said it.

_Speaking of which, this post is getting kind of long, isn't it? Huh._

We're living in the TikTok era, where attention spans are measured in seconds, not minutes. And while there's absolutely still a place for comprehensive content, ignoring micro-content is like ignoring that half your audience is scrolling on their phones during meetings.

Micro-content isn't just "short content"—it's strategically bite-sized pieces designed for immediate consumption and high shareability. Think of it as content snacking between the full meals of your longer pieces.

It fits perfectly into the gaps of your audience's day—the elevator ride, the coffee line, the three minutes before a meeting starts. When someone doesn't have time for your 45-minute webinar, they might still have time for your 60-second tip video.

Plus, micro-content is content marketing on easy mode. That statistic that took you hours to research? Turn it into a shareable graphic. That key insight buried on page 12 of your whitepaper? Make it a standalone social post.

### [38\. Lean into user-generated content (UGC)](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#toc-heading-2f524f11-f527-4a8d-b996-8581d1082967)

Your customers are creating content about your brand whether you like it or not. The question is: are you going to leverage it or ignore it?

User-generated content isn't just free material—it's authentic social proof that outperforms your polished marketing copy every single time. When [Nielsen reports that 92% of consumers trust peer recommendations](https://www.businessnewsdaily.com/2353-consumer-ad-trust.html#:~:text=The%20power%20of%20word%2Dof,when%20making%20a%20purchasing%20decision.) over advertising, they're basically telling you to stop talking and let your customers do it for you.

The smartest brands don't just collect UGC: they actively shape it by providing creative frameworks. Starbucks' White Cup Contest didn't just ask for random photos. It gave clear parameters that resulted in on-brand artistic expressions.

UGC creates a virtuous cycle. When customers see you featuring their peers, they're more likely to contribute their own content, creating a sustainable ecosystem of authentic marketing material.

### [39\. Localize your content](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#toc-heading-d58d04e5-f9d0-40f2-9915-c40917994f7a)

That "universally appealing" content you're so proud of? It's probably alienating half your global audience.

True content localization goes way beyond running your blog posts through Google Translate and calling it a day. It's about recognizing that different markets have fundamentally different needs, references, pain points, and cultural contexts.

When your American case study references baseball metaphors and Super Bowl ads, you're losing your international audience faster than you can say "cultural imperialism," (and that's a mouthful already).

Localization isn't just for enterprise companies. Even if you're a small business, your digital content reaches global audiences. Google Analytics probably shows international traffic you're not effectively serving.

Start small if needed. Identify your top international markets and localize your highest-performing content first. Then expand as you see results.

Just please, for the love of global commerce, stop assuming everyone gets your references to "American as apple pie" or understands your payment processor that only works with US banks.

### [40\. Beat the SEO research](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#toc-heading-713eefa4-aa7b-47fe-acb9-a4fbcfb1f2f9)

By the time a keyword shows decent volume in Ahrefs or SEMrush, you're already too late to the party. The competition has arrived, the difficulty has spiked, and you're fighting an uphill battle for rankings.

Elite content marketers don't chase keywords—they predict them. They identify emerging topics before they hit the research tools and establish authority while everyone else is still wondering if there's an opportunity.

The content teams that master this approach build _massive_ authority while competitors are still waiting for "sufficient search volume" to justify creating content. By the time everyone else jumps on the trend, you're already ranking #1 with established backlinks and engagement signals.

Take "conversational commerce" as an example. Brands that created definitive content when it was just a concept mentioned at tech conferences dominated the SERP by the time it became a high-volume search term.

This approach requires confidence and strategic risk-taking. You'll occasionally invest in topics that never take off. But when you're right (which you will be if you're truly connected to your industry), the payoff is fantastic.

## [Content marketing best practices checklist](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/content-marketing-best-practices\#span-stylefontweight-400content-marketing-best-practices-checklistspan)

We've covered a lot, so we decided to help you out by condensing everything into a quick checklist.
